dedupe_keys.name: a model predictive scheduling strategy for coordinated inland vessel navigation and bridge operation

description: Segovia, Pablo and colleagues publish this resource through the source community. The control-oriented model encodes vessel and bridge-operation logic as inequality constraints and computes coordinated bridge openings and vessel passage times. Coverage is a realistic Rhine-Alpine corridor case. A related rolling-horizon mixed-integer formulation explicitly takes vessel widths and voyage plans and addresses cascaded bridges. These are grouped as related scheduling formulations, without asserting identical source code or benchmark cases. The mathematical scheduling resource is distinct from the separate SMPL lock-placement model. Zenodo supplies the descriptive publication with open access under cc-by-4.0. The publication does not establish public access to an implementation or its separate licence. A limitation is that complete implementation or measurement settings cannot be reconstructed from descriptive metadata alone. Related experimental components and publications retain their distinct roles; separate deposits are not assumed to provide independent observations. The model supports optimisation of coordinated vessel and bridge schedules.
